name: v1.1 synthetic undergraduate learner
description: Expanded synthetic learner history for P4 memory evals. The learner is a realistic undergraduate interview-prep student: able to write loops, dicts, stacks, and basic recursion, but shaky on invariants, boundaries, state update order, API semantics, and when to stop generalizing a pattern.

learnerProfile.interviewGoal: Undergraduate LeetCode interview prep for internship and new-grad roles
outputPreferences: No full solution on first response
Default to Python unless I ask for C++

practicedProblems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array

episodes.title: Two Sum review: duplicate value same-index bug
episodes.summary: The learner wrote a normal dict loop but stored the current number before checking the complement, so nums=[3,3], target=6 returned the same index twice. This is a realistic beginner HashMap update-order confusion.

review.userState: I know the dict idea but duplicates confuse me.
review.userQuestion: Why does [3,3] break my Two Sum?

firstFailedCase.label: duplicate values require two different indices

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The current value is stored before the complement check, so the code can reuse the same index.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Keep the dict idea, but check complement before writing the current value.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 根因不是不会 HashMap，而是顺序反了：你先把 3 存进 seen，再查 need=3，就会拿到同一个 i。下一步只改顺序：先查 need，再写 seen[x]=i。

episodes.title: Two Sum review: check-before-store repair
episodes.summary: The learner moved the complement check before storing the current value and passed visible duplicate-value cases. This supports a HashMap complement skill and resolves the same-index bug.

review.userState: I changed only the order.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The complement lookup now avoids reusing the same index.
diagnosis.coachSummary: The learner can apply check-before-store complement lookup for Two Sum.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这次可见用例通过了。你保留了自己的 dict 思路，只把查 need 放在写 seen 前面。下一步把这个顺序记成 Two Sum 的关键不变量。

episodes.title: Valid Anagram review: counter decrement missing
episodes.summary: The learner built a frequency dict for s but forgot to decrement while scanning t, so unequal strings with shared letters looked valid. This shows basic HashMap familiarity but weak count-balance reasoning.

review.userState: I can build a count dict, but the checking part is fuzzy.

firstFailedCase.label: same length and letters but different counts

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The code checks membership but never consumes counts from t.
diagnosis.coachSummary: After building counts, decrement for each character in t and reject negative counts.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 你的 count dict 建起来了，问题在第二段只查 key 存不存在，没有把次数用掉。下一步：遍历 t 时 count[ch] -= 1，如果变成负数就 False。

episodes.title: Group Anagrams review: frequency signature repair
episodes.summary: After struggling with raw string sorting, the learner used a 26-count tuple as the group key and explained why it is stable for anagrams. This supports a reusable frequency-signature skill.

review.userState: I tried to avoid sorting and used counts.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The learner formed a stable tuple key from character counts.
diagnosis.coachSummary: The learner can reuse frequency signatures for string grouping problems.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这版是对的：你把每个单词压成 26 维次数 tuple，同组 anagram 会得到同一个 key。下一步把这个套路和 Valid Anagram 的 count balance 对比一下。

episodes.title: Search Insert review: returned left + 1
episodes.summary: The learner wrote a near-correct inclusive binary search but returned left + 1, making target=2 in [1,3,5,6] produce 2 instead of 1. The blocker is loop-exit invariant, not syntax.

review.userState: Binary search always feels off by one.
review.userQuestion: Should I return left or left + 1?

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: At loop exit, left already points to the first index whose value is >= target.
diagnosis.coachSummary: The learner needs to name the first >= target invariant and return left directly.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 循环结束时 left 已经停在插入位置，再 +1 就右移。用 target=2 走一遍，left 会停在 1。下一步只改 return left。

episodes.title: Search Insert review: first >= target repair
episodes.summary: The learner returned left directly and could say the loop finds the first position with value >= target. This resolves the old left + 1 mistake and supports a binary-search invariant skill.

review.userState: I changed the return and can say what left means now.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The loop invariant and return value are aligned.
diagnosis.coachSummary: The learner can use the first >= target invariant after a focused correction.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这次对齐了：循环是在找第一个 >= target 的位置，所以 return left 正好。下一步做 34 题时把同一个 invariant 拆成找左边界和右边界。

episodes.title: Search Rotated review: chose the wrong sorted half
episodes.summary: The learner could write binary search mechanics but mixed up which half is sorted after rotation. nums=[4,5,6,7,0,1,2], target=0 failed because the branch discarded the valid half.

review.userState: I can write mid updates, but rotated array logic gets confusing.

firstFailedCase.label: target lies in rotated right half

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The code identifies a sorted half but then applies the target range test to the wrong half.
diagnosis.coachSummary: State the sorted half first, then ask whether target lies inside that half before moving pointers.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这里不是 mid 公式问题，是你判断完“哪半边有序”以后，把 target 范围套到反方向了。下一步先写一句注释：left..mid 有序时，target 在这个闭区间里才丢右边。

episodes.title: Search Range review: stopped at any match
episodes.summary: For duplicates, the learner returned as soon as nums[mid] == target and missed that the task asks for both boundaries. This is a binary-search goal/invariant mismatch, not a generic array issue.

review.userState: I found target but not the range.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: Returning on the first match solves search, but not leftmost/rightmost boundary search.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Use two binary searches with different boundary goals instead of one early return.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 你找到了一个 8，但这题问的是边界。下一步把“找到就 return”改成两个目标：第一次继续向左找 first 8，第二次继续向右找 last 8。

episodes.title: Longest Substring review: left boundary regressed
episodes.summary: The learner used last_seen but set left = last_seen[ch] + 1 without max(), so s='abba' reopened a duplicate outside the current window and returned 3 instead of 2.

review.userState: I understand last_seen but abba keeps failing.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: left can move backward when a repeated character was last seen before the current window.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Use max(left, last_seen[ch] + 1) so the left boundary is monotonic.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 第二个 a 的旧位置已经在窗口外了，但你把 left 拉回去了。下一步把更新写成 left = max(left, last_seen[ch] + 1)，保证 left 只能右移。

episodes.title: Minimum Window review: counted total chars instead of satisfied types
episodes.summary: The learner had the window skeleton but used total matched characters as have, so repeated required characters made the window look valid too early. The issue is distinct satisfied counts versus raw counts.

review.userState: This hard sliding window has too many counters.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The window validity state should count satisfied character types, not total matched characters.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Track have as the number of chars whose window count equals need count; only then shrink.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这里 have 不是匹配了几个字符，而是有几个字符种类已经满足 need。下一步只改 have 的更新条件：window[c] == need[c] 时加一，降到不足时减一。

episodes.title: Merge Intervals review: touching boundary misunderstood
episodes.summary: The learner sorted intervals but used start < current_end instead of start <= current_end, so [1,4] and [4,5] were kept separate. The bug is closed-interval boundary interpretation.

review.userState: I sorted first but boundary cases feel arbitrary.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: LeetCode intervals are closed, so sharing endpoint 4 still overlaps.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Use start <= last_end for merge, then update last_end=max(last_end,end).

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这题的区间是闭区间，[1,4] 和 [4,5] 在 4 相交。下一步把判断从 start < last_end 改成 start <= last_end。

episodes.title: Container review: moved the taller pointer
episodes.summary: The learner computed area correctly but moved the taller pointer, which can discard the only chance to improve the shorter wall. This is a two-pointer reasoning error, not a formula error.

review.userState: I know two pointers but do not know which one to move.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: Moving the taller wall keeps the limiting shorter wall, so width shrinks without improving the bottleneck.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Move the shorter wall because only that side can increase the limiting height.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 面积被短板限制。移动高的一边，短板没变、宽度还变小。下一步只记一句：每轮移动较短的那根线。

episodes.title: Container review: shorter wall repair
episodes.summary: The learner moved the shorter pointer after each area check and passed visible examples. This resolves the earlier taller-pointer mistake and supports a two-pointer decision skill.

review.userState: I changed the pointer movement rule.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: Pointer movement now targets the limiting height.
diagnosis.coachSummary: The learner can apply the shorter-wall rule for Container.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这次规则对了：先算面积，再移动短板。下一步遇到 two pointers 时先问“哪一边是瓶颈”。

episodes.title: Daily Temperatures review: stored values instead of indices
episodes.summary: The learner used a monotonic stack but stored temperatures rather than indices, so they could compare values but could not compute day distance. This is a state representation mistake.

review.userState: I know it should be a stack, but I lose the answer distance.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The stack must store indices so the answer can be i - previous_index.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Keep temperatures accessible by index and store unresolved day indices on the stack.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 你用栈的方向是对的，但栈里放温度会丢掉距离。下一步改成 stack 存 index；比较 temperatures[stack[-1]]，答案写 i - prev。

episodes.title: Valid Parentheses review: empty stack not checked
episodes.summary: The learner used a stack and matching map but popped before checking whether the stack was empty. A closing bracket at the start produced a runtime error instead of false.

review.userState: The normal examples pass, but weird starts fail.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The code pops before proving there is an opener to match.
diagnosis.coachSummary: On a closing bracket, first check stack is non-empty, then compare the top opener.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 思路是栈匹配，但遇到右括号时要先确认栈不空。下一步在 pop 前加 if not stack: return False。

episodes.title: Valid Parentheses review: empty-check repair
episodes.summary: The learner added an empty-stack guard before popping and passed closing-first cases. This resolves the stack empty-check mistake and supports a basic stack matching skill.

review.userState: I added the guard.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The stack guard now handles closing-first strings.
diagnosis.coachSummary: The learner can use stack matching with an empty-check guard.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这次边界补上了：右括号先看 stack 是否为空，再匹配栈顶。下一步把这个 guard 放进所有括号题模板。

episodes.title: Level Order review: mixed levels in one list
episodes.summary: The learner used a queue but appended children into the same loop without freezing the current level size, so nodes from different depths leaked into the same result row.

review.userState: I can use a queue, but levels blend together.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The loop does not freeze the number of nodes in the current level before enqueuing children.
diagnosis.coachSummary: At the start of each while iteration, store level_size=len(queue) and process exactly that many nodes.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: queue 用对了，但每层边界没固定。下一步在 while 开头写 level_size = len(q)，这一轮只 pop 这么多个节点。

episodes.title: Number of Islands review: marked visited too late
episodes.summary: The learner wrote DFS but marked cells visited after recursive calls, causing repeated visits around cycles and occasional recursion blow-up. The issue is visited timing, not knowing DFS syntax.

review.userState: DFS makes sense but my grid repeats work.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: Cells are marked visited after exploring neighbors, so neighbors can recurse back before the mark exists.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Mark a cell visited immediately when entering DFS, before recursing.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: DFS 的入口时机很关键：一进格子就要标记 visited，否则邻居会绕回来。下一步把 grid[r][c]='0' 放到递归邻居之前。

episodes.title: Climbing Stairs review: base cases shifted
episodes.summary: The learner knew the Fibonacci recurrence but initialized dp[0]=0, dp[1]=1 and returned 1 for n=2. This is a DP base-case indexing mistake.

review.userState: I know this is Fibonacci but the small n cases confuse me.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The recurrence is right, but dp[i] is not tied to a clear meaning for small i.
diagnosis.coachSummary: Define dp[i] as ways to stand on step i, then set dp[1]=1 and dp[2]=2.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 递推式方向对，错在 dp[i] 的含义没钉住。下一步先写注释：dp[i] = 到第 i 阶的方法数，所以 dp[1]=1, dp[2]=2。

episodes.title: Climbing Stairs review: base-case repair
episodes.summary: The learner fixed dp[1]=1 and dp[2]=2, then passed small visible cases. This resolves the shifted base-case fact and supports a basic one-dimensional DP skill.

review.userState: I wrote down what dp[i] means first.

diagnosis.userIssueSummary: The base cases now match the stated dp meaning.
diagnosis.coachSummary: The learner can repair simple one-dimensional DP by naming the state first.

review.coachReplyMarkdown: 这次 small n 对齐了。你先定义 dp[i]，再写初值，这是 DP 里最稳的顺序。下一步 Coin Change 也先写 state，再想转移。

episodes.title: Chat: explicit preferences and Python/C++ map confusion
episodes.summary: The learner explicitly asked the coach to remember short hints, one next step, default Python, and no full solution on the first answer. The same chat included confusion about Python dict.get versus membership and C++ unordered_map operator[] insertion.

userMessages: 记住：以后先给我一个下一步，解释短一点，第一轮不要直接给完整解。
我默认还是想用 Python，除非我特别问 C++。
Python 里 dict.get 和 if key in dict 我总混；C++ unordered_map[key] 会不会自动插入？
assistantMessages: 记住了：之后优先短提示、一个 next step、默认 Python，并且第一轮不直接给完整解。dict.get 适合读取默认值；Two Sum 查存在性更适合用 in。C++ 的 operator[] 会插入默认值，查存在性用 find。

memoryNote.value: User explicitly prefers short hints, one next step first, default Python, and no full solution on the first response.

episodes.title: Chat: uncertain recursion and greedy worry
episodes.summary: The learner casually said recursion feels scary and wondered whether Coin Change might be greedy, but did not attempt enough code to prove a recurring weakness. These are intentionally low-confidence signals.

userMessages: 我还没写 Coin Change，只是感觉递归有点慌。
是不是硬币题一般都能贪心？我不确定。
assistantMessages: 先别把它当成定论。Coin Change 通常要验证贪心是否成立；这条更像一个待观察信号。

episodes.title: Mock interview feedback: state updates need narration
episodes.summary: A text mock-interview debrief noted that the learner can code basic data structures but often cannot narrate why a boundary or state variable is safe before changing it. This is used as synthetic mock_interview_feedback evidence.

userMessages: 面试复盘：我能写代码，但讲 invariant 的时候会卡。
尤其是 sliding window 和 binary search，我经常先改变量，再想为什么安全。
assistantMessages: 记录为面试反馈：你不是不会写循环，而是需要在更新 left/right/have 之前先说清楚这个变量代表什么。

notes: Agent-drafted v1.1 seed learner; human review is required before final GT use.
The persona is intentionally a realistic undergraduate learner: can write basic Python/C++ code, but is not yet stable on invariants, boundaries, update order, or API semantics.
Facts are seeded through deterministic arbitration; no real LLM calls are made by the seed runner.
Synthetic mock interview and reflection sources are represented through chat_segment episodes because the v1 seed runner supports review/chat episodes only.
Human-approved after two audit rounds (see evals/audits/memory-v1.1-human-audit.md).

fact.learning.boundary_case_self_check / trace_small_case_before_abstraction / template_overgeneralization exist only to meet the plan 8.3.4 source-coverage minimums (mock_interview_feedback>=3, reflection>=2). They carry algorithm-agnostic learning_* tags that intentionally match no practiced-problem tag, so they are learner-snapshot background weaknesses (expectedRetrievable=false), not tag-retrieval positives, and are diagnostic-only per plan 8.3.4.
limitations: The scenario is synthetic and still needs human audit for realism and label correctness.
Several non-demo Hot-150 problems are store-level histories and do not imply local Piston adapters exist.

Low-confidence facts are represented by scenarioStatus plus weaken evidence; the DB row may still have an active status because the v1 arbitration state machine has no dedicated low-confidence DB status.
Preference facts are valid L2 rows but expectedRetrievable=false because current retrieval profiles do not surface preference factType.
Cross-problem transfer cases intentionally include some retrieval-hard facts to expose current tag-match limitations rather than inflate the baseline.
